advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider the hardcoded `== 75` arm-count assertion; it forces a test edit on every command add/remove and duplicates the real conformance guard.
evidence: Comment claims a guard that under-counts "would silently pass while arms went undocumented" — but test_no_arm_is_undocumented_after_the_fix (line 39-40) already fails in exactly that case, so the exact-count assertion adds churn, not coverage.
Verified count is currently 75 (53 help arms + 24 _INTERCEPTS − 2 overlaps audit/metrics), so the assertion passes today but couples the test to a number that changes with any dispatcher change.
advisory.finding: test_guard_derives_all_seventy_five_arms hardcodes `assert len(dispatcher_arms()) == 75`, which will fail on EVERY future command addition (or removal) even once the new command's doc row is correctly added — a brittle tripwire that is also redundant with the real conformance guard (test_no_arm_is_undocumented_after_the_fix), whose failure would already catch an under-counted arm set that left arms undocumented.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider guarding the reverse direction (documented rows with no live dispatcher arm) so a removed/renamed command's stale doc row is also caught.
evidence: The doc calls itself "the single source of truth" (docs/exit-codes.md:5); a row for a deleted arm is as much a source-of-truth defect as a missing row, but is not guarded.
ABSENCE: no test asserts `documented_arms() - dispatcher_arms() == set()` (modulo the deliberately-excluded meta rows).
advisory.finding: The conformance oracle only asserts arms ⊆ documented (undocumented_arms = arms - documented). It never checks the reverse, so a documented per-command row for a subcommand that has been removed/renamed (a dangling doc row) passes silently — the doc can drift stale in the removal direction without CI noticing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion for the reverse direction (documented_arms() - dispatcher_arms() == set(), modulo intentionally-excluded meta rows) so a stale/typo'd command row also fails CI.
evidence: undocumented_arms is a pure one-directional set-diff: `return arms - documented` (test_exit_codes_doc_conformance.py:38)
test_every_dispatcher_arm_has_an_exit_code_row asserts only `not missing` where missing = undocumented_arms(arms, documented_arms()) (test_exit_codes_doc_conformance.py:43-46)

Concrete failure path: rename/remove a subcommand -> known_subcommands()/_INTERCEPTS drop it, but its lingering row in docs/exit-codes.md (e.g. one of the 34 added rows at docs/exit-codes.md:133-166) is never flagged; documented_arms - dispatcher_arms is never computed.
advisory.finding: The conformance guard only checks arms MISSING a doc row (arms - documented) and never the reverse: a documented row for a command that no longer exists (a removed/renamed arm) or a typo'd arm name is never detected, so a stale/incorrect row persists silently despite the doc's 'single source of truth' claim.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a companion test asserting `documented_arms() - dispatcher_arms()` is empty (excluding the deliberately-listed meta rows), so a documented row without a live arm also gates.
